supplemental_signals.outlook_drift_10k_to_10q: MODERATE — 10-K (Feb 27) bullish on continued M&A improvement; Q1 10-Q (Apr 24) adds tariff-volatility slowdown qualifier; no withdrawal of guidance, no cut to dividend.

summary: Moelis is a textbook 'boring middle' name — the -23% pre-cutoff drawdown looks driven by macro/tariff-cycle re-rating (April 2025 Q1 10-Q acknowledges tariff-induced M&A slowdown and revenue-timing risk) rather than any forensic distress. The 10-K passes every honesty-detector check: 17-year Deloitte tenure with unqualified opinion, no going-concern language, no material-weakness disclosure, zero funded debt, $412M cash and $204M broker-dealer net capital (815x regulatory minimum), undrawn revolvers, disclosed SEC off-channel settlement and Atlas Crest / Stockholders-Agreement litigation all cross-anchored in EDGAR FTS. Form 4 activity clusters to the annual vest/comp cycle, not opportunistic selling. The one meaningful Mode-B finding is outlook drift between the Feb 10-K (confident 'continued improvement') and the April 10-Q (tariff slowdown delaying revenue timing), but that drift was disclosed honestly in the very next filing, which is the opposite of a lying-detector signal. Comp ratio bouncing 63%->84%->69% across FY22-24 is the only UNVERIFIABLE flag — discretionary-bonus accrual could mask earnings smoothing, but is also consistent with normalization after the FY23 revenue trough. Verdict: LONG-tier within boring_middle (clean disclosures, real Q1 inflection, sentiment-driven drawdown).
